label: <DEL> in length-3 sequences containing l/k/v/h/i/r/2/3
explanation: Very sparse update-gate unit. It fires only at step t=3 or t=4 and never in the copy phase. 89% of activation mass is on the <DEL> input, mostly when L=3 (83% of mass; 5% of L=3 delimiter steps fire), with a weaker tail at L=4 <DEL>. The rest (11%) is on the 4th original token at t=3 in longer sequences, mostly when that token is e, z or g. Within L=3 delimiter steps, whether it fires depends on the content of the prefix: it needs some of l, k, v, h, i, r, 2, 3 among the three originals. Magnitude grows with how many of these there are; the top examples, e.g. v l i, l k r, l h i, contain two or three. It does not fire on <DEL> at L>=5, on copy-phase steps, on repeated tokens (in_first=0), or on L=3 prefixes made of other letters (e.g. p w s, a q n). The predicate covers the main L=3 <DEL> mode (dev F1 0.55, mass recall 0.81) and misses the t=3 original-token and L=4 tails.
